newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikon's 96/97 current profit seen lower - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nikon's 96/97 current profit seen lower - paper.

text.p: Parent current profit at Nikon Corp in the year to March 31, 1997 may be about 17 billion yen, 10 percent less than that of a year ago, due to smaller-than-expected investment in semiconductor-producing machines by chip makers, a Japanese newspaper said on Tuesday.
Nikon spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, however, added that Nikon's parent current profit in the six months to September 30, 1996 would be about 10 billion yen, up from its actual half-year parent current profit of 5.09 billion yen in the year ago.
Nikon earlier this year said that it expected 1996/97 parent current profit of 23 billion yen against its actual current profit of 18.85 billion yen in 1995/96.
Japan's major chip makers have already revised down a planned increase in output of semiconductor chips this year due to the sluggish chip market. Chip prices have fallen due to an excessive supply.

On Monday, another major maker of chip-producing machines Tokyo Electron Ltd lowered its parent and group profit forecast for the 1996/97 business year due to chip makers' cut in their production plans.
